title: Annotatio V §.I: both true (Jn 6); PRIOR oral cannot deny carnal; critic’s dual lapse
pass_a_gloss: Each eating, both Proper and Improper, is true — if not by the truth of the signifying thing, yet by the truth of the thing signified. Of the truth of the prior Eating no one doubts; of the truth of the posterior Christ’s Discourse in John 6 lets no one doubt. The PRIOR, as by pleonasm it is called Oral, since it can be done only with the mouth; so it is denied to be Carnal only by contradiction, since what is oral, insofar as such, cannot but be acknowledged carnal, the human mouth being at least in part numbered with man’s flesh. So that in one and the same eighth paragraph someone disputing is caught slipping not once and simply, when he judges Supernatural eating opposed indeed to the Carnal and Capernaite, but not to the Oral — as if the Oral were not Carnal, or Capernaite at least in part and insofar as it is Oral; and then holds Oral and True Eating as synonyms, as if Spiritual Eating done by faith alone were not true.
pass_b_english: Both proper and improper eating are true (by the thing signified). John 6 settles the improper’s truth. The PRIOR / Oral cannot without contradiction be denied Carnal — the mouth is flesh.
A disputant in one §.8 slips twice: opposing supernatural only to Capernaite/carnal but not to oral, and treating Oral and True as synonyms — as if faith-alone spiritual eating were not true.
source_text: Utraque, tam Propria, quàm Impropria, manducatio vera est, si non veritate rei significantis, tamen veritate rei significatæ. De veritate prioris Manducationis nemo ambigit; De veritate posterioris neminem sinit ambigere Sermo Christi Joh. 6. PRIOR, uti, per pleonasmum, Oralis dicitur, cùm non nisi ore fieri possit; Ita non, nisi per contradictionem, omnino negatur esse Carnalis, cùm quod orale est, eatenus, quatenus tale, non possit non carnale agnosci, ore humanô hominis carni, ex parte saltem, annumerando. Ut proinde, unô eodemque paragraphô octavô, non unâ & simplici vice lapsus deprehendatur non nemo disputans, quando tùm Supernaturalem manducationem Carnali quidem & Capernaiticæ, non item Orali, oppositam censet: quasi verò Oralis, Carnalis non esset, aut Capernaitica, saltem ex parte & quatenus Oralis est; tùm Oralem, & Veram, Manducationem, pro synonymis habet, quasi verò Spiritualis Manducatio, solâ fide peracta, non esset vera?
notes: Both true; oral=carnal; critic’s dual lapse.
